lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Reception. The lobby smells like new carpet over an old building. A wall of awards, none dated later than eighteen months ago.

lines.speaker: joan
lines.text: Morning. You'll be the new project manager? Mike E. is expecting you — go on up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She says it plainly, the way she'd say it to anyone. She doesn't know you yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You take the stairs. Posters at every landing insist you're curious, brave, together. Nobody's checked if that's still true.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Upstairs, the office is quieter than a company mid-crisis has any right to be. A desk near the window still has a mug on it — half-full, gone cold. Nobody's moved it. Nobody's sitting there either.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You made it. Good — we need every pair of hands we can get right now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She's already gone before you can answer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mike E. is waiting, door open. He doesn't get up.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You must be the new PM. Ellis's replacement.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A beat. He says the name like it costs him something small every time.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Sit down. Before you ask me anything—

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: —tell me what you think is wrong with this project.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He watches you. Not impatient. Testing.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Because something clearly is. You just haven't found it yet.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: That's not important right now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He looks back down at the folder on his desk, like the conversation's already over.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: What's important is whether you can tell me what's wrong with this project. Start looking.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Good. Start wherever you like. Emails, Teams, the shared drive — it's all a mess, take your pick.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He hesitates, like there's a second sentence he's deciding whether to say.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The Board wants an update in six days. I'd rather you found the problem before they did.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He turns back to his screen. The conversation, such as it was, is over — but you notice he still hasn't touched the mug.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You get read access to Ellis's old inbox — nobody's reassigned it yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You get added to the Steering Group channel Ellis used to be in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A message pops up in the corner of your screen.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: That's useful, but it's scattered. If you want the full picture, it's in SharePoint — Project NOVA's own folder. I can point you there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He drops a link. The breadcrumb at the top reads: Group Tax Innovation & Change › 4. Managed Projects › 11. Project NOVA.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You navigate to the project's SharePoint folder.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Fine. That's the external picture. What about us?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He nods at the corkboard behind him — half-empty, waiting.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats. Yours to fill in. Don't flatter us.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player builds the SWOT.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You lay it out plainly: a Board that trusts speed over process, a Quality lead nobody's briefed properly yet, and a delivery team that hasn't worked together before this week.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...You're not wrong.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You go looking for the original Business Case to check it against what you've found. The main document opens fine. The appendices don't exist.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You search Ellis's old email account. Then Teams. Then the shared drive again — further in this time, past the folder you already found.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Buried three folders deep: a partially finished document. "Benefits_Plan_DRAFT_v3." Last edited nine days before Ellis resigned. It stops mid-sentence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tucked behind it, a single scanned page — handwriting, not typed. A notebook page, out of place among the spreadsheets.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “They want a plan. What they need is someone who'll tell them the truth before it's too late.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't know yet what that means. You have a feeling you're going to.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: So. What's your diagnosis?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Monday. The coffee machine is doing that thing again — the one where it decides sugar is optional whether you asked for it or not.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You look like you survived the Board.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A small laugh, more relief than humour.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Barely, right? Mike E. was in a mood all morning. Something about scope.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She takes her coffee, pauses.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You'll figure out fast that nobody here agrees on what this project actually needs. Buckle up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She's gone before you can ask what she means.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By the time you reach the boardroom, you understand. This was never just a construction project. Somewhere between the concrete and the contract, it became a negotiation.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Right. Let's get this done. Everyone's had the requirements list — today we decide what actually gets built.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Every automation line on that list is a Must. I'm not being dramatic — the throughput targets don't work without them.

lines.text: Every one of those "Musts" has a number next to it, Priya. I've added them up. You're proposing we double the budget before we've poured a foundation.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: And validation isn't on that list at all yet. I'd like to fix that before we talk about anything else.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: One thing at a time. You're chairing this — talk us through it.

lines.text: [Player drags requirements into Must / Should / Could / Won't. The room watches the board fill in. Nobody says anything until it's done.]

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You've just doubled the budget.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: So automation's a "Should" now? That's going to hit us in commissioning, not now — when it's expensive to fix.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Automation as a Must. Thank you — that's going to save us weeks in commissioning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Camille cuts in before Mike E. can respond.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Actually — I'd rather we under-build automation than under-build validation. We can automate a working line later. We can't un-fail an inspection.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The room goes quiet. Mike E. looks between them — this isn't a fight he called.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...Noted, Camille. Final call. Does the board stand as it is, or are you changing it?

lines.speaker: daniel

lines.speaker: daniel

lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: This doesn't reflect who actually had authority over this project. Neither Daniel's budget nor Camille's quality sign-off is where you put them.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Third. The isolator delay, early in delivery — how was that resolved, and what did it cost?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You show the expedite approval, dated, costed, signed off the same day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You show the revised schedule, and the message where you told Mike E. it would slip, in writing, before it slipped.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Either's defensible. What isn't defensible is doing one and reporting the other. You didn't. Noted.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Last one. Do any of your own status reports say something the rest of the record doesn't support?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whitfield opens {mismatchReportLabel}. “{mismatchDimensionLabel} — {mismatchReportedRag}.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She sets it beside what was actually true that week: {mismatchEvidence}.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Walk me through that judgement.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't have a good answer. There isn't one.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: This one concerns me more than the others.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whitfield opens {mismatchReportLabel}. “{mismatchDimensionLabel} — {mismatchReportedRag}.” Against it: {mismatchEvidence}.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Walk me through that judgement.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You give her the reasoning — not a full picture, but not nothing either. A call someone could have made in good faith.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Defensible. Barely.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whitfield checks all three reports against what was actually true, each time. Doesn't find anything.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: No, they don't. That's rarer than you'd think.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: That's everything I need for today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player reviews the evidence exhibit.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She doesn't say anything else. Inspectors generally don't.

DIALOGUE_ACT5_SCENE03.engineNote: This scene is fully dynamic, not scripted branching — every condition reads directly from gameState.flags (filling_line_approved/deferred/rejected from ACT4_SCENE02; daniel_power_recognized/camille_power_recognized from the Act 3 stakeholder grid; isolator_expedited/isolator_absorbed from ACT4_SCENE01) or from effectiveDialogueFlags' synthetic report_mismatch_material/borderline/consistent (see findMostMaterialReportMismatch in state.ts, which replaced the old hid_problem_from_marcus boolean this build — see the "Act 5 build" entry in DESIGN_NOTES.md). {mismatchReportLabel}/{mismatchDimensionLabel}/{mismatchReportedRag}/{mismatchActualRag}/{mismatchEvidence} are template tokens from reportMismatchTemplateValues, same substitution mechanism as {currentWeek}/{chosenSupplier}. has_reputation_tag's closer was cut for this build — nothing in the engine populates gameState.reputation.tags yet (see DESIGN_NOTES.md); revisit once reputation is built as the cross-game feature world_memory.json describes, not just an inspection line. No dice roll, no hidden randomness — entirely a readout of the player's own decision history, per design intent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inspector Whitfield's team leaves without a word about outcome. That's normal. It still feels like something.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The office doesn't quite know what to do with itself. Nobody starts a new task. Nobody quite finishes an old one either.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mike E. stands by the window, not really looking at anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Priya reorganises the same folder three times.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Camille reads the same page for what must be the fourth time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody says the word “inspection” out loud for the rest of the day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The phone rings.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mike E. answers it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't speak. He listens. For a long time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then he slowly smiles.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Fade to black.]

DIALOGUE_ACT5_SCENE04.engineNote: No choices, no UI copy, no player input — per Tab 9 UI Copy v2, this screen intentionally has zero text chrome around it. Auto-advance to ACT6_SCENE01 after the cinematic completes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: THREE WEEKS LATER.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The building looks finished now, in the way buildings only look finished once people are actually using them instead of building them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Facility Progress final reel plays: Week 1's empty warehouse through to Week 24's medicine on the line, side by side.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inspector Whitfield was never testing your memory. She was testing your paperwork — because paperwork is just decisions, written down so someone else can trust them later.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You're about to find out if yours held up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before any of that, though: an email from Procurement, subject line clinical.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: NHS PROCUREMENT — CONTRACT UPDATE. Due to the revised delivery date, the exclusivity window could not be held. NOVA remains eligible to bid in the next procurement cycle.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody in the room reacts to it yet. There's still a batch to run.

DIALOGUE_ACT6_SCENE01.engineNote: contract_lost is read from lib/nova/endings.ts's evaluateEnding() Contract Gate (Gate 1) — see DESIGN_NOTES.md's 'Four-family ending architecture' entry. Deliberately placed here, not withheld until ACT6_SCENE03, per design brief: the player should feel the commercial loss before finishing the facility, not only in the final ending screen — "do you still deliver professionally?" is the point. Minimal by design: no reaction beats, no player choice, just the notice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everyone who can fit is in the control room. Mike E.. Camille. Vaughn — and, if you did right by him, his daughter, hovering near the back, trying not to look as nervous as she clearly is. Priya. Daniel. Tomasz. Aisha.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Vaughn keeps glancing toward the door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The line starts.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Silence. Nobody talks over the hum of equipment actually running, for the first time, doing the thing it was built to do.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Screens show the batch progressing. Green, then green, then green.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Quality Control waits with the rest of you. Waiting is apparently the same for everyone, regardless of job title.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Finally — results.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: BATCH RELEASED.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Someone — you're not sure who first — starts clapping. Then everyone does.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...Right. Go on, all of you. You've earned five minutes of this before I put you back to work.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: BATCH REJECTED.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The clapping that was already starting dies half-formed.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: It's a quality flag, not a catastrophe. We find out why, and we fix it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...Right.

DIALOGUE_ACT6_SCENE02.engineNote: batch_released / batch_rejected are now read from lib/nova/endings.ts's evaluateEnding() Quality Gate (Gate 2) — regulatoryReadiness/riskExposure plus findMostMaterialReportMismatch's severity, not a standalone formula (see DESIGN_NOTES.md's 'Four-family ending architecture' entry; supersedes this note's old END-1..7 mapping). vaughnTrust_high gates the daughter cameo, consistent with the plant in ACT3_SCENE01.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: NHS contract's confirmed. Board's thrilled. For what it's worth — I wasn't sure anyone could actually pull this off. Including you, some weeks.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ellis couldn't, in the end. You could. I don't say that to make you feel good. I say it because it's true — and I don't like surprises, remember.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Contract's secured. Margin's thinner than what we promised the Board, but it's real.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't smile exactly. More like the absence of worry, which on Daniel passes for the same thing. The team looks like people who won something that cost more than they expected.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Contract's secured. I'll be honest, I fielded more questions about this one in the last three weeks than I did about the whole rest of the programme.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The control room is quieter than you'd expect for a project that just succeeded.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The facility launched. The Board signed off, but the questions didn't stop there — some doubt about your judgement never quite went away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The facility launched. The team got there, but they're running on fumes — this win took more out of them than it should have.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The facility launched. The numbers held up under Whitfield's inspection, barely — and ‘barely’ has a way of following you into the next project.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The facility launched. But too much goodwill had been spent getting it there — delivery succeeded, even if some of the people you needed along the way were less convinced by how you got there.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: We lost it. Competitor got there first.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You told me the truth the whole way through, even when it cost you. That's worth more to me than the contract, and I mean that — though I'd rather have had both.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There will be another project. This one's just over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first batch fails on a technicality. Camille has the root cause identified within the day — your documentation made it fast.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Second batch, three weeks. This is fixable. It's fixed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The batch fails, and the evidence trail is too thin to explain why quickly. The Board pauses the programme pending external review.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I have to reassign you. This isn't personal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It doesn't feel like it's not personal. You think, not for the first time, of Ellis's desk. The mug that never got moved.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The building works. The politics didn't. A rival executive, whose name you can now put to several small moments of friction over the last six months, has quietly had you moved off the project before launch.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I fought this. Same as before.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You believe him. It doesn't change anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The concern nobody addressed properly in Act 4 became a formal external investigation, and it overtook the project's own timeline entirely.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody in the control room is celebrating today. They're answering questions instead.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here's what the building remembers about you:

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — Joan's greeting, this morning, whatever it was.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — Vaughn's site crew, waving or not waving, the last time you crossed the floor.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — Daniel, auditing your figures or trusting them outright.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — A Board member, somewhere, quoting a decision you made months ago back to you as though it were obvious.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — The status report Inspector Whitfield asked about, and whether it held up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the Benefits Register — Ellis's draft, finished with Daniel back in Act 3:

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ✓ NHS Contract Secured — realised.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ✗ NHS Contract Secured — not realised.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ⚠ More Patients Treated — ENABLED, measurement continues post-launch. A released batch proves the line can manufacture at volume; it doesn't yet prove a single patient has been treated. That's a monthly production-output number nobody in this room has seen yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ✗ More Patients Treated — NOT YET ENABLED. No batch means no output to measure. This benefit doesn't start until one does.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ⚠ £12M Investment Justified — not yet measurable. Per the Register: {roiMeasure}, evidenced by {roiEvidence}, due {roiWhen}. Nobody in this room gets to know that answer today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Register never did say anything about Product B. That gap is still sitting there, open, whatever happens today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Final cost: {forecastCostFormatted} against the {approvedBudgetFormatted} approved — {costPerformanceLabel}. What that spend actually bought is the question above; this is only whether you kept to what you were given.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Late, packing up the last of your things from the desk you've had for months now, you find one more page. The last one.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “I thought if I just held the line long enough, it would hold itself. It didn't. Whoever reads this — you'll do better. Or you won't. Either way, nobody does this one perfectly.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ellis Grant wasn't removed for being a bad project manager. They were carrying the exact same pressures you just survived — sponsor expectations, regulation, budget, constant change — alone, for far longer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You didn't beat Ellis. You survived the same project.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Project management was never about finding the perfect answer. It was about making informed decisions, under real pressure, with people who didn't always agree with you — including the ones who turned out to be right, and the ones who turned out to be wrong, including yourself.

DIALOGUE_ACT6_SCENE03.engineNote: Retagged for the v2 gate-based ending architecture (lib/nova/endings.ts's evaluateEnding, see DESIGN_NOTES.md's 'Four-family ending architecture' entry) — supersedes this note's old END-1..7/single-composite description. The 7 condition flags below (ending_TRIUMPHANT_LAUNCH, ending_PYRRHIC_financial, ending_PYRRHIC_political, ending_PYRRHIC_scrutiny, ending_PYRRHIC_recoverable_quality_failure, ending_CONTRACT_LOST, ending_BATCH_REJECTED) are mutually exclusive and come from endingConditionFlags(state) in lib/nova/endings.ts, not stored on gameState.flags. Dialogue TEXT is unchanged from the old END-ids this pass (retagging only) — one known mismatch worth a future content pass: the ending_PYRRHIC_scrutiny block's text ("overtakes the project's own timeline entirely... answering questions instead") was written for the old END-7's binary override and reads more severe than its new trigger (a stakeholder-goodwill dip that did NOT cross the Contract Gate's severeGoodwillFloor — a severe-enough dip now routes to ending_CONTRACT_LOST instead, with ACT6_SCENE01's new NHS Procurement notice, and reuses ending_CONTRACT_LOST's existing text rather than this block). The world memory reel and closing line always render, after whichever single ending block played. all_ellis_fragments_found = true only if fragments 1–6 are all in gameState.flags. BENEFITS REGISTER READOUT (reworked alongside the benefitsRealisationScore retirement — see 'Benefits system rework' in DESIGN_NOTES.md): this now reads status off the Benefits Register artefact's own Measure/Evidence structure (lib/nova/artefacts.ts's benefitsRegister entry, completed in Act 3 via TOOL_ACT3_SCENE06_BENEFITS) rather than a numeric score that only ever moved downward. contract_secured/contract_lost are from endingConditionFlags — read directly off the Contract Gate result, not derived from which ending band fired. batch_released/batch_rejected likewise reuse the flags ACT6_SCENE02 already renders against, but the More Patients Treated line is now deliberately NOT a clean ✓/✗: a released batch proves manufacturing capability, not that any patient was actually treated (that's a post-launch, monthly-production-output measurement the game's timeline never reaches) — so batch_released reads ⚠ ENABLED / measurement continues, and only batch_rejected (no batch, no capability, nothing to measure) reads ✗ NOT YET ENABLED. The ROI line always renders unconditionally, and now pulls {roiMeasure}/{roiEvidence}/{roiWhen} from benefitsRegisterTemplateValues(state) in lib/nova/state.ts — a read of TOOL_ACT3_SCENE06_BENEFITS's own correctMeasure/correctEvidence/correctWhen fields for the ROI benefit, so this line can never drift out of sync with what the Act 3 tool actually asked the player to prove. The optional Product B line is gated on second_product_benefits_undefined, a real gameState.flags entry (not a synthetic endingConditionFlags one) set only when CHOICE_BIG-01's 'phase_b_quietly' option is chosen — see that choice's own engineNote for why only that option, not full_replan or renegotiate, genuinely leaves Product B's benefits undefined. COST-PERFORMANCE LINE (added alongside the CBS classification rework/budget reconciliation pass, always renders unconditionally right after the benefits block): {forecastCostFormatted}/{approvedBudgetFormatted}/{costPerformanceLabel} come from budgetReconciliationTemplateValues(state) in lib/nova/state.ts, fed via GameRoot's templateValues the same way {currentWeek} already is. Deliberately its own line, not folded into or offered as evidence for the ROI line above it — cost performance (stayed inside the approved £12M) and investment justification (was the spend actually worth it) are different questions; conflating them was the exact mistake this pass was designed to avoid. See the 'Budget reconciliation — Gate 3 financial subscore + HUD + Act 6' entry in DESIGN_NOTES.md.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Week {currentWeek}. Everything's been going well.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mike E. doesn't sit down.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I need five minutes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't wait for a response.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The Board closed on an acquisition this morning. A generics manufacturer — Corvane Pharma.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He lets that sit for a second longer than feels comfortable.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: They want NOVA to manufacture Corvane's flagship product as well. Both lines. Same facility. Same timeline.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Silence.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Both? Mike E., we costed one product line. Not two.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I know what we costed, Daniel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He turns to face the player directly.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I fought this. I lost. The Board's already told the market — this is happening. The only question left is how.

DIALOGUE_BIG-01.engineNote: {currentWeek} = the live HUD week number at the moment this scene fires (derived from scheduleHealth via the weeksRemaining formula, NOT a hardcoded value — this is intentionally whatever the player's actual playthrough has produced by this point, same template-substitution pattern as EV-R1's {chosenSupplier}). Also: this scene should set flag second_product_benefits_undefined = true on completion (any of the 3 choices) — read by the HUD to surface a new 'Second Product Benefits: Undefined' line once BIG-01 resolves.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three hundred and forty-one unread. Ellis stopped answering two weeks before he left.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You open Teams. The project channel goes quiet exactly nine days before the resignation email.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The PID. Half-finished, but finally in your hands.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Well? What have you found?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Tomorrow's Board meeting isn't routine. They want to know if anything's changed outside these walls since the business case was approved.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He slides a folder across the desk. It's thin. Thinner than a project this size should have.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Steel. Regulation. Funding. Demand. Somebody upstairs is going to ask if any of it still holds up. I'd like an answer that isn't "we didn't check."

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: So — which lens do you want to look through?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player tags PESTLE factors: new environmental regulations affecting construction, global shortages of specialist stainless steel, government funding incentives for UK pharmaceutical manufacturing, and demographic-driven demand growth.]

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...That's more than I expected you to find in a day.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Good enough to start with.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He stands, finally, jacket already half on.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: One thing. Never surprise me. Whatever you find from here — however bad — I hear it from you first. Not from the Board. Not from a status report I'm reading in the room.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He holds the door.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Don't make me regret hiring Ellis's replacement twice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whatever you chose, it's the first real crack in a plan that looked, three weeks ago, like it might hold together cleanly. It won't be the last.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Later that week, clearing space for a new supplier folder, you find something that isn't a supplier folder. Another page, same handwriting as before.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “Scope only ever grows. Budget for that, not for the plan you were given.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You fold it into the growing stack of things Ellis apparently knew and never got to act on. You wonder, not for the first time, whether knowing was ever really the problem.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Report two. More of the picture is visible now than it was a month ago — not all of it good.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: How's my project?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player fills out the Status Report.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Weeks pass. Under a plan that now covers two products instead of one, the pressure doesn't land evenly — some of it lands exactly where you'd expect, some of it doesn't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The pace doesn't let up. Some of what was only ever a line on a register months ago stops being theoretical.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The contractor risk stops being a line on the Risk Register. It's an issue now, and it needs a record, not just a reaction.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player updates the RAID log.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A third report, and the project has history now — reports one and two are both still on file, whatever they said.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: How's my project? Inspector Whitfield's going to ask the same question soon enough — I'd like our answers to match.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player fills out the Status Report.]

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: The cleanroom design failed GMP review. Not close. Failed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She lets it land before continuing.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: We can rework it now, appeal the finding, or phase the fix around commissioning and hope nobody asks before we're ready.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: Residents are complaining about the construction traffic. Local paper's asking questions.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Investors are coming. Not next quarter — Thursday.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He already looks like he's rehearsing something in his head.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Contamination. During commissioning. I need a decision, not a discussion.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: The electrical contractor's gone under. Actually gone, this time.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: At least we saw it coming.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Loading bay's flooded. Half the delivered equipment's sitting in six inches of water.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: New MHRA guidance dropped this morning. We need to check we still comply.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: Supplier shipped the wrong voltage spec. Whole pallet.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: Problem with the equipment from {chosenSupplier}. Nothing catastrophic — but it's not what we were promised.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You think, briefly, about the ones you didn't choose.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Funny thing about the budget you didn't spend on the extra filling line — turns out it's exactly what's needed now, with everything else that's landed on you since.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: I know I've pushed back on nearly everything you've proposed. For what it's worth — on this one, I think you're right. I'll back you with the Board if it comes to that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: News breaks that one of the suppliers you passed over — the fast, expensive one — has gone into administration after over-promising on a rival's contract.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel doesn't say “I told you so.” He doesn't have to.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Good instinct on the budget, actually.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: We do not have enough validation resource for two product lines on this timeline. That's not a risk. That's arithmetic.

lines.speaker: aisha
lines.text: Ravi just resigned. Effective immediately.

lines.speaker: aisha
lines.text: Elin just resigned. Effective immediately.

lines.speaker: aisha
lines.text: One of the automation engineers just resigned. Effective immediately.

DIALOGUE_ACT3_SCENE06B.engineNote: HUD activates here for the first time, showing Est. finish Week X/24 (derived from scheduleHealth, see scene note), plus Budget/Delivery Pace/Risk/Quality/Benefits and a Current Objective line (derived from the Milestone Gantt built in ACT3_SCENE04). HUD retires once Act 5 begins. The badge line above is deliberately NOT phrased as 'Week 1/24' — scheduleHealth (and therefore the HUD's own Est. finish figure) can already have drifted from its 100 baseline by this point via earlier Act 2 choices, so a literal 'Week 1' claim here could contradict the HUD's own number on the very next screen. The two closing sublines (added per the Act 5 attainability audit — see DESIGN_NOTES.md) are this game's one deliberately explicit, HUD-tutorial-adjacent moment: they establish that Delivery Pace/Quality have hard floors worth protecting, without stating the actual numbers (40 / 70 — those live in the HUD's own colour bands, not in prose) so they age gracefully if the thresholds are ever recalibrated. Risk is deliberately NOT covered here — already legible from its own HUD band, and made sufficiently explicit later in the game on its own terms. Later scene-level choice copy (e.g. Act 5's readiness interventions) stays narrative-only on top of this — players are expected to combine a choice's plain-English framing with what they already know from here and the HUD, not be shown raw +/- deltas a second time.
